prompt:
Image 1 is the grid of grey clay figures to paint over: keep every figure exactly where it is, at exactly its size, pose, facing and camera, and paint each one as the rider and horse of Image 2 seen from behind; no clay may remain. Keep the 4 by 4 layout of Image 1, with no grid lines drawn, and its flat pure green (#00FF00) background.
Image 2 is the approved painted portrait of this rider and horse: use it only for its identity, its colours, its materials and its marks, painted in the same hand. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing, its dark background, its candlelight or its facing; every figure is the whole rider and horse, small in its cell, exactly as large as its clay figure.

A game sprite sheet: 16 full-length painted figures of one Ash Rider on his Ash Horse, seen from behind, one figure in each cell of a 4 by 4 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure green (#00FF00) background. The same rider and horse, the same colours and the same scale in every cell; only the pose changes.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at miniatures on a table; orthographic, no perspective, so every figure is the same size. Every figure faces away from us, toward the upper right of the image, exactly as its clay figure does: we see its back, its right side and the top of its head; no face is seen. The figures are foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head and the back large, the legs short; never at eye level, never seen from the side.

Light: outdoor daylight. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side of the rider and horse with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows, nothing glows unless the description says so. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, the same hand as the painted portrait reference; a muted earthy palette with the rider and horse's own colours exactly as its portrait shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette that still reads when shrunk to 60 pixels. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The figures: An Ash Rider of the Cinder Horde on his Ash Horse. The horse is the horse of Image 2: a heavy dark ash-grey warhorse, bred to carry, not to fight, with paler ash dappling on the neck and a greyer muzzle; a thick soot-black mane falling on the near side, a soot-black forelock and tail; a riveted plate of dark iron with rusted edges and a short blunt ridge down its middle over its face from the brow to the nose; a bridle of blackened leather with iron rings; a caparison of dull ember-orange cloth bordered with a charcoal band, covering its back and rump from the saddle to the tail and hanging low on both flanks. The rider: a lancer in blackened iron scale with a dull ember-orange shoulder cape, a rounded dark iron helm with a dull ember-orange horsehair crest, ash-grey skin, a long ash-wood lance with a dark iron head and a dull ember-orange pennon just below it, a sword at the hip (in the windup and strike cells the sword is in his hand and the lance is gone). Its marks, every one painted clearly: the riveted iron face plate; the soot-black mane and forelock; the ember-orange caparison with its charcoal border; the iron bridle rings; the greyer muzzle; the dark ash-grey coat with paler dappling. Seen from behind and above, the caparison over the horse's back and rump, the soot-black tail, the rider's cape, crest and lance show; the faces are hidden.

Side colour: dull ember-orange (#C4532C) cloth on the horse's caparison over its back, rump and flanks, the rider's shoulder cape and helmet crest, and the lance pennon: large, clean, unbroken areas that face the sky and the camera, so that a wedge of these riders reads as that colour from far away. The rest stays muted iron, charcoal and ash grey.

Facing, again: every figure in every cell faces the same way as its clay figure, away from us toward the upper right, including the hit figure and the falling one; no face is seen anywhere on this sheet.

Scale: A rider and his standing horse together are about 62% of the cell's height; riderless and lying figures keep the same scale.

The cells, left to right, row by row (the poses of the clay figures):
1. (row 1, column 1) the horse standing square, the rider sitting upright, the lance held upright.
2. (row 1, column 2) walking: one diagonal pair of legs forward.
3. (row 1, column 3) walking: the other diagonal pair forward.
4. (row 1, column 4) galloping, fully extended: front legs reaching forward, hind legs stretched back.
5. (row 2, column 1) galloping, gathered: all four legs bunched under the body.
6. (row 2, column 2) the charge: the horse at full gallop, the rider leaning forward behind the couched lance, aimed at the enemy.
7. (row 2, column 3) the horse standing, the rider with the sword drawn far back, body twisted.
8. (row 2, column 4) the horse walking, the rider slashing down with the sword.
9. (row 3, column 1) hit: the horse rearing back, the rider knocked back in the saddle, arms out.
10. (row 3, column 2) the horse collapsing, the rider tumbling off its back.
11. (row 3, column 3) the horse lying dead on its side, the rider lying dead beside it.
12. (row 3, column 4) the horse and the rider lying dead, a different sprawl.
13. (row 4, column 1) the horse alone without its rider, bolting at a gallop, extended.
14. (row 4, column 2) the horse alone without its rider, bolting at a gallop, gathered.
15. (row 4, column 3) the horse standing, the rider raising the lance high overhead.
16. (row 4, column 4) no figures: only the lance lying flat on the ground, as dropped.

Background: one flat pure green (#00FF00) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow; at least 24 pixels of clean background between any two figures and around the edges. No green anywhere on the creature: no green glow, no green reflections.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; extra figures; cropped or overlapping figures.
